examples.name: Agent governance golden (offline)
examples.description: schema + validate + @pure helpers + @effects on a tool handler (no LLM key)
examples.learningGoal: Validate tool/LLM-shaped payloads and mark pure vs effectful helpers before side effects.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints normalized summary/steps, then an invalid: validate error.

examples.name: Phase 6 pure + validate (unit)
examples.description: Minimal @pure helper + validate() on a tool input schema
examples.learningGoal: See the smallest offline unit of governance used by CI smoke.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a normalized name from validated tool input.

examples.name: Single Agent - Code Generator
examples.description: Agent that generates code
examples.learningGoal: See the simplest complete MALDA agent workflow after prompts.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints generated code returned by an agent.

examples.name: Multi-Agent Code Review
examples.description: Writer and reviewer agents working together
examples.learningGoal: Understand how MALDA scales from one agent to multiple collaborating roles.
examples.expectedOutput: Runs two agents with separate responsibilities.

examples.name: Declarative agent team (offline)
examples.description: agents.team binds role specs to a directed graph; handoff validates an edge contract
examples.learningGoal: Declare multiple agents and their relations as data, then validate a hop without an LLM.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints member count, writer role, handoff rel, then true/false/false for contract checks.

examples.name: Declarative agent kinds (offline)
examples.description: agents.define kind selects CodingAgent / HumanAgent / DevAgent tool bundles without downloading a model
examples.learningGoal: Pick a specialized agent class from a spec instead of listing tools by name.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints CodingAgent, HumanAgent, then true for unknown-kind reject.

examples.name: Team plan hops (offline)
examples.description: executePlan(plan, team) rejects a dependsOn hop that is not a declared relation, before any LLM call
examples.learningGoal: See the team graph as an allow-list for plan hops, not just handoff().
examples.expectedOutput: Prints true — reverse Writer hop is rejected.

examples.name: Team handoff think flag (offline)
examples.description: team.handoff fourth argument stays validate-only when false; true would call to.think(payload)
examples.learningGoal: Keep handoff offline by default; opt into to.think only when you pass true.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints true / true / true — validate-only hops, no response field.

examples.name: Team review and reject (offline)
examples.description: team.review / team.reject require matching rel; { approved: false } records a verdict without an LLM call
examples.learningGoal: Use typed review and reject hops instead of treating every edge as a handoff.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints true / true / false / true / true / false.

examples.name: Team plan verdicts (offline)
examples.description: executePlan think: false branches reject hops on step.approved without an LLM call
examples.learningGoal: See a rejected review take the reject hop and an approved review skip it.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints 3 / 0 / 2 / rewrite.

examples.name: Team consult (offline)
examples.description: team.consult requires rel: consult; one-shot ask that does not transfer the plan
examples.learningGoal: Ask another role without a handoff or review verdict.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints true / which API? / false / false.

examples.name: Agent with File Reading Tool
examples.description: Agent that reads files using tools
examples.learningGoal: Show how MALDA agents gain practical power through tools.
examples.expectedOutput: An agent reads files and responds based on their contents.

examples.name: Agent with File Editing Tool
examples.description: Agent that edits files using tools
examples.learningGoal: Advance from read-only tools into controlled agent-driven editing.
examples.expectedOutput: Uses an agent to modify files through MALDA tools.

examples.name: Multi-Agent File Workflow
examples.description: Multiple agents collaborating with file tools
examples.learningGoal: See MALDA's commercial automation story in a more complete collaborative workflow.
examples.expectedOutput: Runs multiple specialized agents over a file-based workflow.

examples.name: Complete Agent-Based Refactoring
examples.description: Full workflow: read, analyze, refactor code files
examples.learningGoal: Showcase a more production-shaped agent automation flow.
examples.expectedOutput: Performs a complete agent-based refactoring workflow.

examples.name: Agent with Grep and Insert Tools
examples.description: Agent that searches files and inserts content at specific lines
examples.learningGoal: Demonstrate a more targeted tooling workflow for advanced users.
examples.expectedOutput: Uses search and targeted insertion tools from an agent.

examples.name: Agent with User Input Tool
examples.description: Agent that can ask questions to the user
examples.learningGoal: Introduce human-in-the-loop workflows without jumping to large production demos.
examples.expectedOutput: The agent asks the user questions and continues with the answer.

examples.name: MALDACodingAgent - MALDA Development
examples.description: MALDACodingAgent for MALDA script development with file tools, MALDA execution, and compilation
examples.learningGoal: Expose MALDA's premium developer-platform angle once the learner already understands basic agent concepts.
examples.expectedOutput: Runs a MALDA-focused agent workflow with execution and compilation support.

examples.name: Second Brain
examples.description: CodingAgent explores docs, distills a hierarchical second-brain note tree, then answers questions or generates downloadable documents from it (OpenRouter or local LLM).
examples.learningGoal: Build a personal knowledge base from a docs folder and query it with an agent.
examples.expectedOutput: Interactive BUILD/ASK flows with optional Generate document download; optional compile with --embed-folder secondbrain.

examples.name: Second Brain (semantic)
examples.description: Same BUILD as Second Brain, but ASK retrieves notes via GraphMemory (vector + BM25 hybrid) and can generate downloadable documents. Compare with secondbrain.malda for synonym/paraphrase search.
examples.learningGoal: See how GraphMemory + embeddings improve ASK over lexical token overlap on the same distilled notes.
examples.expectedOutput: Interactive BUILD/ASK with GraphMemory index; place bge-m3-Q4_K_M.gguf beside the script/exe for multilingual neural retrieval.
